name: Lightning Bolt
label: Load Records
lede: Two Brians from a Providence art school set up on the floor wherever the crowd happens to be: one on a bass strung with banjo strings, one drumming with a telephone mic strapped inside a mask.

eras.title: Three kids and a textile mill
eras.text: Lightning Bolt starts at the Rhode Island School of Design as an improvising trio that tours without bothering to record. Home is Fort Thunder, a warehouse in Providence's Olneyville district where Brian Chippendale and friends live, draw comics, wrestle in costume and put on shows.

years.h: Two Brians meet at RISD
years.p: Drummer [[Brian Chippendale|2de5109e-2713-46dd-8de5-f64ee000da49]] hears about a new kid who is a whiz on bass and goes looking. He finds [[Brian Gibson|0aa47f69-47f0-4bf4-a445-8756df8e3d42]], and Lightning Bolt starts in Providence.

years.h: Hisham Bharoocha joins after the first gig
years.p: A RISD student, [[Hisham Bharoocha|724cb291-89dd-4b9f-a968-d7d4531ad66d]] adds percussion and vocals. The trio improvises its sets and tours without recording anything.

years.cap: Fort Thunder show poster, Arab On Radar and Lightning Bolt
yt: Fan footage of a Fort Thunder show, 1997
years.h: Chippendale and Mat Brinkman take the second floor of a mill
years.p: The pre-Civil War textile mill in Olneyville becomes home, studio and venue for Fort Thunder, and for Providence's noise and comics underground.
years.xp:
The original residents were Mat Brinkman, Chippendale, Rob Coggeshal and Freddy Jones. Fort Thunder became known for dense, colorful screen-printed posters, costumed wrestling nights and Halloween mazes, as well as shows.

Its alumni went on to noise bands, alternative comics and galleries. Forcefield, the art collective born there, showed at the 2002 Whitney Biennial.

years.h: Bharoocha leaves for the band that becomes Black Dice
years.p: He quits for another RISD band, soon to be [[Black Dice|d8f9a4bd-ec27-4e29-8b3e-b8bdb62f950e]]. His only released Lightning Bolt track is Revenge, on Load's Repopulation Program compilation.

eras.title: Down on the floor
eras.text: As a duo, Chippendale and Gibson work out the setup that makes them: a bass tuned like a cello, drums pounded under a shriek through a telephone receiver. Load Records talks them into making records, but they never trust the studio, and the live show stays the point.

years.h: Ben McOsker asks for a record
years.p: Until Load Records founder Ben McOsker approached Chippendale and Gibson in 1997, Lightning Bolt had never thought about writing songs to record.

years.h: The debut: 750 copies on Load
years.p: Lightning Bolt cut five studio tracks, threw out four, and swapped in lo-fi live tapes from 1997 and 1998.

q: Be super loud and you're all set.
years.h: The band skips the stage and plays on the floor
years.p: The crowd forms a tight circle around Chippendale's kit and Gibson's amps. Lightning Bolt has also played kitchens, sidewalks and parking lots.
years.xp:
Sometimes they started seconds after the opening band finished, before anyone had moved. Chippendale sings through the microphone from a household telephone receiver, held in his mouth or strapped inside a mask, and runs it through effects and a KMD 8021 Drum Exciter.

Gibson tunes his bass to cello tuning (C G D A), puts banjo strings on the high end, and later moved to five strings. Volume, he said, solved most problems.

years.h: Ride the Skies gets a real studio
years.p: The second album is the first made more or less the normal way, not stitched together from live tapes.

yt: Ocean State Media on Chippendale and Fort Thunder
years.h: Fort Thunder is evicted and razed for a Shaw's
years.p: After two years of protests and court challenges, the collective is forced out. Developer Feldco levels the mill for a supermarket and a Staples parking lot.
years.xp: Wikipedia says both stores closed soon after opening. The demolition set off an argument over development and gentrification in Olneyville, the poorest neighborhood in Providence.

eras.title: Best alarm clock ever
eras.text: The records get clearer, the crowds get bigger and the critics catch up. The band crosses oceans, gets turned back at one border, and Chippendale drums for Björk.

years.h: Wonderful Rainbow, Load No. 41
years.p: Recorded in Providence and Costa Mesa with Dave Auchenbach, it's the band's catchiest record. Pitchfork later ranked it No. 157 of the 2000s.
years.xp: It's also in 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.

years.h: The Power of Salad puts the band on DVD
years.p: Peter Glantz and Nick Noe direct a film about Lightning Bolt.

q: Best alarm clock I've ever had.
years.h: A noon set on John Peel's doorstep
years.p: At All Tomorrow's Parties, Lightning Bolt sets up at noon outside DJ [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]]'s chalet. That's Steve Albini's verdict, from next door.
years.xp:
The festival housed its bands in holiday-camp chalets, so a guerrilla set could happen anywhere. Albini of [[Shellac|604f273a-d3c1-4b5b-ab83-99541f9368ea]] and [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]] was the neighbor.

Peel died that October.

years.h: Frenzy, promised for the end of summer, never arrives
years.p: A post on the band's website said an improvised album by that name was in the works at Load. It never came out.

years.h: Hypermagic Mountain goes straight to DAT in a house
years.p: Recorded between May 29 and June 21, half in a studio and half in a Providence house, to 2-track DAT. Metacritic ranked it fifth among 2005's albums.
years.xp:
Chippendale made the cover art first; the title came after. Engineer Dave Auchenbach caught the house sessions with no multitrack at all.

Alternative Press gave it five stars and NME 9/10. Pitchfork's Brandon Stosuy called it the band's most well-oiled album.

years.cap: Lightning Bolt live with the crowd around them, c. 2006
years.h: Japan sends the band home after 48 hours
years.p: Fresh from a UK tour, Lightning Bolt is detained on arrival for lacking work permits. The appeal is rejected and they are sent home.

years.cap: Lightning Bolt at the Magic Theater, Omaha, April 2007
years.h: Björk hires Chippendale
years.p: He drums on her album Volta, then on a 2008 charity single.

years.h: Two Lightning Bolt drummers in a field of 77
years.p: At the [[Boredoms|0798d15b-64e2-499f-9969-70167b1d8617]]' 77 Boadrum in Brooklyn on 7/7/07, Chippendale plays drummer No. 77. Ex-member Bharoocha is musical director.

years.h: Earthly Delights closes the Load years
years.p: The fifth album is the band's last full-length for Load Records, and its last for almost six years.

eras.title: Other careers, then a cleaner signal
eras.text: Lightning Bolt goes quiet on record while both members build second careers: Chippendale in comics and art, Gibson in games at Harmonix and then his own studio. When the band comes back, it's on Thrill Jockey.

years.cap: Brian Gibson and Brian Chippendale at Le Grim
years.h: Metacritic puts the Providence duo eighth for the decade
years.p: Its Artists of the Decade 2000-09 list places Lightning Bolt at No. 8.

years.h: Chippendale's comic If 'n Oof and a show in Brooklyn
years.p: The comic comes out in 2010, and that June he shows art in "Fruiting Bodies" at Cinders Gallery. Ninja and Maggots came before; Puke Force follows in 2016.

years.h: Oblivion Hunter collects 2008 leftovers
years.p: The band's first EP, on Load, gathers unreleased material recorded in 2008.

years.h: Fantasy Empire, and for the first time you can hear everything
years.p: The first album on Thrill Jockey streams on NPR's First Listen on March 9. NPR praises a clarity and fidelity the earlier records never had.
years.xp: The nine songs end with the 11-minute Snow White (& The 7 Dwarves Fans). Metacritic scored it 84.

years.cap: Lightning Bolt at Carson Creek Ranch, Austin, May 2015
years.h: Gibson leaves Harmonix to start a game studio
years.p: After working as a lead artist at Harmonix since 2001, he quits in summer to found Drool with Marc Flury.

years.h: Thumper, a rhythm-violence game with Gibson's art and music
years.p: Drool releases it in October to critical acclaim.

years.h: Rolling Stone lists Chippendale at No. 91
years.p: Rolling Stone's 100 Greatest Drummers of All Time puts him there.

eras.title: Back, and still loud
eras.text: The seventh album arrives after four more years, with song titles as absurd as ever. Chippendale keeps side projects going, including a duo with Ty Segall.

years.h: Sonic Citadel ends on Van Halen 2049
years.p: The second Thrill Jockey album runs 11 songs, from Blow to the Head to USA Is a Psycho.

years.h: Chippendale and Ty Segall start Wasted Shirt
years.p: Chippendale and [[Ty Segall|07a17571-81fc-4cf8-a634-98f0d926d313]] release Fungus II as the duo Wasted Shirt.
